C0.quote: the aggregation of individual preferences into a collective choice
C0.note: Group-theoretic analysis of symmetry (anonymity/neutrality) of social preference functions; a procedure aggregating voters' linear orders.

C1.quote: we completely solve the neutrality problem
C1.note: Characterisation of which groups arise as symmetry groups of spfs; algebraic/axiomatic (anonymity, neutrality).

C2.1.quote: The ordered list of the individual preferences is called the preference profile.

C2.2.quote: We then assume that each individual i ∈ H expresses her preferences

C2.3.quote: Individual preferences are expressed by relations on a set N
C2.3.note: Individual preferences are referred to, but they are identified with the input.

C2.4.quote: We then assume that each individual i ∈ H expresses her preferences
C2.4.note: The preference profile is the input of the spf and is applied directly; no statement about reporting or sincerity.

C3.1.note: No strategic misreporting is analysed; strategy-proofness is only mentioned in the introduction as an example property.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Results concern symmetry groups. Efficiency appears only in the introduction when recalling Moulin's theorem.

VOT.note: Individuals are only indices of the profile; they take no actions in the model.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

C9.1.note: The abstract, introduction and conclusion make claims about mathematical results only, and about relations to Boolean function representability. They make no claims about institutions, voter well-being, or which rule to use.

C10.1.note: No statement of a procedural reading or of taking no position on inputs versus held attitudes.
